DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position [L4]:** Jesus Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost without any man's seed. Joseph was his father only by supposition and by law, not by begetting. The Hebrew and Greek words below are tied to the KJV verses quoted with them.

---

## 1. The genealogy stops "begat" at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L3]** Every earlier link in the chain uses the same word, as in Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."

**[L2]** The verb behind "begat" in both verses is *gennaō* (ἐγέννησεν, to beget). In Matthew 1:16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called *anēr* (ἀνήρ, husband or man) "of Mary". The relative pronoun "of whom" is *hēs* (ἧς), which is feminine singular, so it can only refer to Mary and not to Joseph. The birth verb is passive, *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη, was born).

**[L4]** The chain "X begat Y" runs unbroken until Joseph. It then says Jesus was born "of whom", meaning Mary alone. The feminine pronoun in Matthew 1:16 and the repeated "begat" in Matthew 1:2 together show that the verse withholds the verb of begetting from Joseph and assigns the birth to Mary.

## 2. The source of the conception is stated

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Came together" is *sunerchomai* (συνέρχομαι, to come together, to cohabit). "Of the Holy Ghost" is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου), where *ek* (ἐκ) means "out of" and marks the source. "With child" is *en gastri echousa* (ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα, having in the womb).

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Conceived" is *gennēthen* (γεννηθέν, begotten or generated). The same *ek* appears again: the child is *ek pneumatos* (out of the Spirit).

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The verb *ginōskō* (γινώσκω, to know, a term for marital union) is imperfect, *eginōsken* (ἐγίνωσκεν), so Joseph was not knowing her up to the birth.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy "before they came together". Matthew 1:20 gives the source as "of the Holy Ghost". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until the birth. Together these exclude a human begetter. The source is named, the time is fixed before cohabitation, and the whole period up to the birth is covered.

## 3. Mary's question and the answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "Man" is *anēr* (ἀνήρ, a male person, husband). "Know" is *ginōskō* (to know carnally). The present tense, *ginōskō*, shows she was not then in marital union with any man.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (ἐπισκιάζω, to cast a shadow over, to envelop). "Therefore" is *dio* (διό, for which reason), so the title "Son of God" follows from the conception described.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". The word *parthenos* (παρθένος, virgin) is fixed in the record before the conception in Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**[L4]** Mary asks how, "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). The reply offers no human union. It names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and it states the result with "therefore also" (Luke 1:35). The answer to her question is therefore a conception that does not come from a man.

## 4. The prophecy fulfilled

**[L1]** Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel."

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew word behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (H5959, a maiden). **[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses the same word, rendered "virgin", of Rebekah at the well, whom Genesis 24:16 describes as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done" so that the prophecy would be fulfilled. Isaiah 7:14 speaks of a virgin conceiving, and Genesis 24:43 and 24:16 show the word applied to a woman no man had known. Matthew therefore presents the conception as a virgin's, with no man's seed.

## 5. Joseph is "supposed" the father, and Christ corrects it

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** "Was supposed" is *enomizeto* (ἐνομίζετο, was thought or reckoned), from *nomizō* (νομίζω, to think, to hold as opinion). It marks a popular belief and not a fact.

**[L3]** Luke 2:48: "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:49: "And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" Christ answers Mary's "thy father" with "my father's".

**[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the crowd's belief. Matthew 1:20 reports Joseph being told otherwise, and Luke 3:23 labels the crowd's belief "supposed".

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels Joseph's fatherhood "supposed", and Luke 2:49 has Jesus redirect "thy father" to "my father's". These verses mark the crowd's belief in John 6:42 as an opinion Scripture itself corrects.

## 6. Davidic descent does not require Joseph's seed

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L2]** "Seed" is *sperma* (σπέρμα, offspring or descendant). The word is used of the woman in **[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." So *seed* can descend through a woman.

**[L1]** Luke 1:31-32: "Thou shalt conceive in thy womb... the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 shows "seed" reckoned through the woman. Romans 1:3 says Christ was made "of the seed of David according to the flesh". Together they allow a Davidic descent through Mary's conception without Joseph's seed. Luke 1:31 places the conception in her womb, and Luke 1:32 gives "father David" as the line of the throne.

## 7. The body was prepared

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** "Prepared" is *katartizō* (καταρτίζω, to fit out, to make ready). It is a verb of divine making.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35 gives the method as the Holy Ghost coming upon her.

**[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body. Luke 1:35 gives the method in Mary. The pair match the account of a conception without a man's seed.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew's genealogy withholds "begat" from Joseph and assigns the birth to Mary alone. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16 and Matthew 1:2; [L2] *gennaō* (to beget) and the feminine *hēs* (of whom, feminine singular).
2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost", before Joseph and Mary came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit) and *sunerchomai* (to come together); [L3] Matthew 1:25.
3. Mary was a virgin who knew no man, and the angel's answer gave the Holy Ghost as the cause. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34-35; [L2] *anēr* (man), *ginōskō* (to know carnally) and *episkiazō* (to overshadow); [L3] Luke 1:27.
4. The conception fulfils Isaiah's virgin sign. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:22-23 and Isaiah 7:14; [L2] *ʿalmāh* (H5959, maiden); [L3] Genesis 24:43 and Genesis 24:16.
5. Joseph is called father only by supposition and by law, and Christ himself points to another father. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed); [L3] Luke 2:48-49 and John 6:42.
6. Davidic descent and the prepared body do not need a human father's seed. Footing: [L1] Romans 1:3; [L2] *sperma* (seed or offspring) and *katartizō* (to prepare); [L3] Genesis 3:15 and Hebrews 10:5.
7. Therefore Christ had no human biological father. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of, source); [L3] Matthew 1:25.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# CHALLENGER, ROUND 1: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David

**Position [L4], footed on the chain below:** The flesh of the child came as the promise required it, "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3), "of the fruit of his loins" (Acts 2:30). The one man the text names as husband, as father and as "son of David" is Joseph. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the origin God claims for the child he calls his son. It is the same marker the text puts on men who have fathers.

---

## PRESSES AGAINST THE DEFENDER'S DECLARED CHAIN

### PREMISE 1, against LINK D1: "of whom was born" names the mother. It fits a named husband.

**PRESSED WITH:** Matthew 1:16; Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13; Galatians 4:4.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." The same verse that carries the passive gives Joseph as "the husband of Mary."

**[L2]** The verb *egennēthē* (was born) with *ex hēs* (out of whom, feminine) names the woman who bore the child. *Anēr* (husband, man) is Joseph's word in this row. It is the word Matthew 1:19 gives him: "Then Joseph her husband."

**[L3]** "Born of" a woman is the Bible's way of naming the mother of a man whose father is named. Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." Galatians 4:4 uses the same idiom: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The idiom also runs through Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble."

**[L4]** The passive with the feminine pronoun names Mary as the one who bore the child (L2). The same idiom is used of John, whose father Zacharias is named (L3, Matthew 11:11 with Luke 1:13). So the wording of D1 fits a mother named beside a named husband, which is exactly what Matthew 1:16 prints. D1's reading, "meaning Mary alone," takes the verse further than its own words carry it.

### PREMISE 2, against LINK D2: "Of the Holy Ghost" sits in the row that names Joseph, and the timing rows are Matthew's own order.

**PRESSED WITH:** Matthew 1:20; 1 John 5:1; 1 John 4:7; Matthew 1:24; Matthew 1:25; Genesis 4:1.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20, quoted whole: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" The angel names the husband ("son of David") and the wife ("Mary thy wife") in the same breath as "of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The margin's word is *gennaō* (to beget). The same verb, with *ek* (out of) God, is used of believers in 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]"

**[L3]** 1 John 4:7 uses it again: "every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God." Men with human fathers are "begotten of" God by the same *ek* and the same verb. When Paul means the flesh, he adds the flesh-marker: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

**The timing, in Matthew's order:**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." This dates when she was *found*.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife." This is her coming into his house.
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The word "till" bounds the abstaining to the pregnancy.
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1 gives the canon's stated means of begetting: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."

**[L4]** Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The canon's means of begetting is the husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1). Matthew 1:25 bounds the abstaining by "till" to the time after the taking (Matthew 1:24). On these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. "Of the Holy Ghost," read with 1 John 5:1, marks origin from God and fits a father named in the same row. D2's "exclude a human begetter" rests on reading *ek* as paternity. The *ek* rows do not carry that reading.

### PREMISE 3, against LINK D3: Mary's "know" is present tense, and the angel's verbs are verbs of power and presence.

**PRESSED WITH:** Luke 1:31; Luke 1:32; Luke 1:34; Acts 1:8; Luke 24:49; Luke 9:34; Acts 5:15.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L2]** *Ginōskō* (I know) is present indicative. It states her state at the moment the angel spoke. The conception is future in Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."

**[L2]** *Eperchomai* (to come upon) is the verb of Acts 1:8. **[L3]** Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me." Luke 24:49 describes the same event: "until ye be endued with power from on high."

**[L2]** *Episkiazō* (to overshadow) is the cloud's verb. **[L3]** Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."

**The "therefore":** The *dio kai* (therefore also) in Luke 1:35 connects back to Luke 1:32, not forward to biological divine paternity. Luke 1:32 gives both the title and the throne before Mary asks her question: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

**[L4]** Both verbs of Luke 1:35 are used at their other rows of the apostles being empowered and of the cloud of presence (L2 with L3, Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34). The title rests on the throne promise already given in Luke 1:32. So the angel's answer fits empowerment and presence upon a woman espoused to "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27). D3's "a conception that does not come from a man" reads begetting into verbs whose rows carry power and covering.

### PREMISE 4, against LINK D4: Isaiah's sign shows its own pattern, a woman who conceives by a man.

**PRESSED WITH:** Isaiah 7:16; Isaiah 8:3; Isaiah 8:4; Isaiah 8:8; Proverbs 30:19; Luke 1:27.

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"

**[L2]** *ʿAlmāh* (H5959) stands in 7 verses: Genesis 24:43; Exodus 2:8; Psalm 68:25; Proverbs 30:19; Song of Solomon 1:3; 6:8; Isaiah 7:14. The KJV prints "virgin," "maid" and "damsels" at those verses. At Proverbs 30:19 it is printed "the way of a man with a maid."

**[L3]** Isaiah bounds the sign in his own day:
- Isaiah 7:16: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son."
- Isaiah 8:4: "before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother."
- Isaiah 8:8 names Immanuel in that day: "the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."

**[L4]** The KJV word "virgin" names the woman when the sign is spoken. Luke likewise names Mary "a virgin espoused" (Luke 1:27) before the future "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31). The sign's own first unfolding in Isaiah has a man going to the prophetess, and "she conceived" (Isaiah 8:3). Matthew's "that it might be fulfilled" (Matthew 1:22) stands whole, and it fits this pattern. D4's "with no man's seed" adds a consequence the sign's rows (L1 with L3) present the other way.

### PREMISE 5, against LINK D5: "As was supposed" is a verb of custom, and the narrator and Mary name Joseph father.

**PRESSED WITH:** Luke 2:27; Luke 2:33; Luke 2:41; Luke 2:48; John 1:45; 2 Samuel 7:14; 1 Chronicles 28:6.

**[L2]** *Enomizeto* is from *nomizō*, "properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom ... to deem or regard." **[L3]** It is the same form as Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." The prayer there was real. The word carries custom, not a verdict of error.

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary, who received the angel's word, calls Joseph "thy father."

**[L3]** Luke, the narrator, does the same:
- Luke 2:27: "the parents brought in the child Jesus."
- Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled."
- Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year."

A disciple says it in John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."

**The two fathers in one row:** "my father's business" (Luke 2:49) is the covenant Father of 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." 1 Chronicles 28:6 shows both fathers in one verse: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." David begat Solomon, and God called Solomon his son.

**[L4]** The verb of Luke 3:23 is the verb of custom (L2 with Acts 16:13). Mary and the narrator name Joseph father and parent (L1 with L3). The title "my son" stands beside a begetting father in 1 Chronicles 28:6. So "my father's business" fits a son of God's covenant who has a father in the flesh, as Solomon did. D5's "Christ himself points to another father," offered as a correction of Joseph, sets the covenant Father against the begetting father. The rows hold both.

### PREMISE 6, against LINK D6: The Davidic seed is of loins and bowels, and is reckoned by the house of the fathers.

**PRESSED WITH:** 2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:10; Hebrews 7:14; Numbers 1:2; Numbers 1:18; Genesis 4:25; Luke 1:5; Luke 1:36; Hebrews 2:14; Hebrews 2:16; Hebrews 2:17.

**[L1]** The seed rows:
- 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L2]** *Zera'* (seed, posterity) stands in 2 Samuel 7:12. *Osphys* (loins, procreative power) stands in Acts 2:30. It is the word of Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."

**[L3]** Reckoning is by the father's house:
- Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**"Her seed" in Genesis:** Genesis 3:15's "her seed" is answered by Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son ... For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed." Eve calls Seth her seed, and Adam is his father.

**Mary's kin in Luke:** Luke 1:36 gives "thy cousin Elisabeth." Luke 1:5 places Elisabeth: "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron."

**The prepared body (Hebrews 10:5, "a body hast thou prepared me"):** It stands with Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same." It stands with Hebrews 2:16: "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]." And it stands with Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren."

**[L4]** The seed is to come out of David's bowels and loins (L1 with L2, *osphys*). Tribe is "evident" by the house of the fathers (L3, Numbers 1:2 and 1:18). "Her seed" stands beside a named father in Genesis 4:25. So the Davidic seed of Romans 1:3 is carried down the fathers' line to "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The body God prepared was made "likewise" and "in all things" like the brethren (Hebrews 2:14, 17).

**Question to the defender:** According to Hebrews 7:14, how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given the law of Numbers 1:2 and 1:18, "by the house of their fathers"?

### PREMISE 7, against LINK D7 (keystone)

The keystone stands on D2 and D3, its footing being Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35, *ek* and Matthew 1:25.

- Matthew 1:20 carries "Joseph, thou son of David ... Mary thy wife" in the same row as *ek* (Premise 2).
- Luke 1:35's verbs carry power and presence (Premise 3).
- Matthew 1:25's "till" bounds the abstaining to the pregnancy (Premise 2).

**[L4]** With its three footings pressed by their own rows, D7's "no human biological father" rests on D2 and D3 as read. Those readings do not fit the rows quoted above.

---

## CHALLENGER'S OWN CHAIN

**C1.** The promised seed is flesh out of David's body.
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3.
- [L2] *zera'* (seed), *osphys* (loins), *spermatos* (seed).
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10.

**C2.** Tribe and pedigree are reckoned by the house of the fathers.
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14.
- [L3] Numbers 1:2, 18.
- [L2] *bayith* (house), *'ab* (father).

**C3.** The named father is Joseph, of the house and lineage of David.
- [L1] Luke 1:27; Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David"; Luke 2:48; Matthew 1:20.
- [L3] Luke 2:33; Luke 2:41; John 1:45.

**C4 [L4].** Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are the covenant origin and title.
- Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:19, 20, 24, 25 and Genesis 4:1.
- [L2] *ek* with *gennaō* at 1 John 5:1.
- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 and 2 Samuel 7:14.

# ROUND 2: DEFENDER'S ANSWER (reissued)

**Position [L4]:** The child was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost and has no human biological father. Joseph is father by law, through the naming. Mary's own descent supplies the flesh of David.

---

## ANSWER TO THE QUESTION PUT TO ME (Hebrews 7:14)

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**[L2]** The word behind "evident" is *prodēlon* (G4271, plainly manifest). It states that the fact is manifest: "our Lord sprang out of Juda." The channel by which he sprang is carried by the registers and rows below (Luke 3:23, Luke 3:31, Ezra 2:61).

**[L3]** Numbers 1:2 enrols "every male by their polls" for the muster of the host. Numbers 27:8 provides for descent without a son: "If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter." Ezra 2:61 names a man who "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." So the house of the fathers is a registry, and it was entered through a daughter's line.

**The two registers, Matthew and Luke:**

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** [L4] Jesus Christ had no human biological father. His conception in Mary was the work of the Holy Ghost, apart from any man. Joseph was his legal and reputed father, not his begetter. By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed begets the child. The topic asks whether such a man stands behind Christ. The KJV text answers no.

---

## 1. The text names the source of the conception, and it is not a man

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (out of, from as source) names origin. The same verse fixes the timing: *prin ē synelthein autous*, "before they came together." The pregnancy preceded any union of Joseph and Mary.

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Conceived" is *gennēthen*, from *gennaō* (to beget, to bring into being). This is the same verb the genealogy uses for fathers begetting sons. In Matthew 1:20 its source is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." Where the genealogy has a man as the source, this verse has the Holy Ghost.

**[L3] Matthew 1:2:** "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Here *gennaō* has a human father as source. Matthew 1:20 uses the same verb with a different source.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 each give a source for the conception, and both give the Holy Ghost. Matthew 1:2 shows that when Matthew means a human father he says "begat." Where he means this child's conception he names the Holy Ghost. The chain runs from the source named in 1:18, to the source named in 1:20, to the verb's ordinary use in 1:2.

---

## 2. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link uses the active *egennēsen*, "begat." The final link switches to the passive *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. It cannot point to Joseph. Joseph is called *ton andra Marias*, "the husband of Mary."

**[L3] Matthew 1:12:** "Jechonias begat Salathiel." This is the pattern of "begat" that Matthew 1:16 leaves at Joseph.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:16 carries the line in two ways. It stops using "begat" for the last link, and it makes Mary the one "of whom" Jesus was born. Joseph is placed in the line as husband, not as begetter.

---

## 3. Mary was a virgin, and she says she knew no man

**[L1] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L2]** The word is *parthenos* (a virgin). It is used twice in this one verse.

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (to know, including carnal knowledge) is in the present tense: *andra ou ginōskō*, "I know not a man." Her question is about the way, since she has not known a man.

**[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Episkiazō* (to overshadow) is the word for the Highest's power covering her. The conclusion is introduced by *dio kai*, "therefore also." The child is called the Son of God because of this act of the Holy Ghost.

**[L4]** Mary asks how it can be when she knows no man. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and it gives no man. Luke 1:35 ties the child's identity ("therefore") to that cause and not to a human father.

---

## 4. Prophecy: the sign was a virgin conceiving

**[L1] Matthew 1:22-23:** "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *'almah* (H5959). The Greek in Matthew 1:23 is *parthenos* (a virgin).

**[L3] Genesis 24:43:** "behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." The KJV uses "virgin" here for *'almah*, of Rebekah, whom Genesis 24:16 calls "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** The KJV renders Isaiah 7:14 as "a virgin shall conceive." Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done" to fulfil it. That is two lines of footing for a conception in a virgin and without a man.

---

## 5. The body was prepared by God

**[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** *Katartizō* (to fit, to prepare) is the word for the preparing of the body. The preparer is God, the one addressed.

**[L3] John 1:14:** "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us."

**[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 names God as preparer of the body. John 1:14 says the Word was "made flesh." Neither verse supplies a human father, and both are consistent with Luke 1:35.

---

## 6. Objections the text answers

**Objection A: "His father and mother" (Luke 2:48, and John 6:42).**
**[L1] Luke 3:23:** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
**[L2]** The Greek is *hōs enomizeto*, "as was supposed," from *nomizō* (to deem, to hold by custom or opinion). Luke marks "son of Joseph" as the common opinion and not as fact. John 6:42 ("whose father and mother we know") is the speech of the crowd, which is the same supposition.
**[L3] Luke 2:49:** "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Mary said "thy father," and the child answered with "my Father" in the next verse, pointing to God.
**[L4]** Luke 3:23 itself marks "son of Joseph" as supposed, and Luke 2:49 corrects the language of the household.

**Objection B: "knew her not till" (Matthew 1:25).**
**[L1] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *Heōs* (until) states the limit of the matter Matthew is addressing, which is the birth. Joseph "knew her not" through the pregnancy.
**[L3] Matthew 1:18:** the child was conceived "before they came together."
**[L4]** Matthew 1:25 confirms that the conception was not Joseph's. The birth came first, and the marriage came after.

**Objection C: Jesus is "of the seed of David."**
**[L1] Romans 1:3:** "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
**[L2]** *Genomenou ek spermatos Dauid*: "made out of the seed of David." The verb is *ginomai* (to become). It does not say "begotten by."
**[L3] Luke 1:32:** "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
**[L4]** Luke 1:27 puts Mary and Joseph both "of the house of David," and Matthew 1:16 says Jesus was born "of whom," Mary. Davidic descent through Mary needs no human father.

---

DECLARED CHAIN

1. The Holy Ghost, and not a man, is named as the source of the conception, and the pregnancy came before Joseph and Mary came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:20; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit) and *gennēthen* (begotten, conceived); [L3] Matthew 1:2, where *gennaō* has a human father as its source.
2. The genealogy ends with a break: Joseph is "the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus," not the one who begat. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16; [L2] *egennēthē* (was born, passive) against *egennēsen* (begat, active), and *hēs* (of whom, feminine); [L3] Matthew 1:12, "Jechonias begat Salathiel."
3. Mary was a virgin who knew no man, and the angel's answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the cause. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:27, Luke 1:34, Luke 1:35; [L2] *parthenos* (a virgin), *ginōskō* (to know), *episkiazō* (to overshadow); [L3] Matthew 1:25, "knew her not."
4. The prophecy of a virgin conceiving is applied to this birth. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23; [L2] *'almah* (H5959) rendered "virgin" in the KJV, and *parthenos* (a virgin); [L3] Genesis 24:43.
5. "Son of Joseph" is the supposition of the people, and the child himself names God as his Father. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 and Luke 2:49; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed) from *nomizō* (to deem by custom); [L3] John 6:42, where the crowd says "whose father and mother we know."
6. Therefore Christ had no human biological father: his conception was of the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary, and Joseph was his father only by legal and reputed standing. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of) with *gennēthen* (begotten) and *episkiazō* (to overshadow); [L3] Hebrews 10:5, "a body hast thou prepared me."

# CHALLENGE: The seed of David came through a named father, and the conception rows fit it

**Position.** [L4] Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the husband of Mary, "of the house and lineage of David." The promise requires seed out of a man's loins. The text names that man in four voices. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the canon's language for a begetting by God, a language it uses of people who have fathers. I aim at the keystone **D6** and at the links that carry it: **D1, D3, D5**, and **D2, D4**.

---

## MY DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's loins and is counted by the father's house.**

[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."

[L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

[L1] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

[L2] The words are:
- *zera'* (H2233, seed, posterity) at 2 Samuel 7:12.
- *osphys* (G3751, the loin, procreative power) at Acts 2:30.
- *spermatos* (G4690, seed) with *kata sarka* (according to the flesh) at Romans 1:3.

[L3] Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"

[L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." The loin-word is the same *osphys*, of a father.

[L3] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

[L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Here *'ab* (H1) means father and *bayith* (H1004) means house.

[L4] The promise names bowels, belly, loins and seed "according to the flesh." Hebrews puts the loins in "his father." Numbers counts the tribe "by the house of their fathers." So Christ's springing "out of Juda" is evident by a father's house and a father's loins.
